target_customer: Venture-backed startups and lenders that want to launch their own credit products
problem: Launching a credit product requires building origination, underwriting and loan servicing plus state and federal compliance, which is slow and costly.
business_model: B2B API and compliance platform sold to companies launching credit products (pricing not found)

founders.name: Jessica Zhang
prior_employers: Stilt (chief of staff and product manager)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page; worked on Stilt's B2B credit API product Onbo.

founders.name: Alex Hegevall Clarke
founders.background_notes: Named in TechCrunch and FinTech Global; the YC page lists only a first name.

competitors.name: Setpoint
competitors.what: Software for faster loan transactions, also marketed as a Stripe for credit

technical_complexity.rationale: Origination, underwriting and servicing across many states with compliance guardrails is deep fintech engineering plus legal work.

defensibility.rationale: Licensing and compliance coverage and deep integration into customer lending flows make it harder to copy than a plain API.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent absorbing Pier; a Hacker News thread cited alternatives such as LoanPro, Canopy, Peach and Lendflow.

market_need_then: Founders saw at Stilt how much time and money credit companies spent keeping tech stacks compliant with federal and state rules.

branding.domain_note: Uses pier-finance.com rather than an exact pier.com.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positions as a trusted compliance partner and not a lender

brand_strength.rationale: The Stripe for credit tagline was repeated by TechCrunch and others, but the name is generic and shares search space with Pier Asset Management.

outcome_analysis: Founders came from Stilt and built a compliance-first credit API. They raised a $2.4M seed in January 2024 from YC and others, and a 2026 profile says it keeps expanding. No Series A or customer names are public, so the stage is early and traction is unverified.
notes: Aggregators give totals of $2.4M, $2.9M and $3M and one lists a $500K pre-seed; these are unverified and not recorded as rounds. Seed was reported by FinTech Global, TechCrunch, PYMNTS and Financial IT. Competitor Setpoint is dated January 2024, one year after the batch; no earlier source found. Founding year is reported as 2022 or 2023.
